title: Induction of Type 1 Diabetes and Myocardial Infarction in Rats
author: Michael Hill
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8fmhtk6
materials: Induction of Type 1 DM Type 1 DM was induced in male Sprague–Dawley rats by administering a single intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of streptozotocin (STZ) (65 mg/kg body wt) (Sigma) prepared daily in citrate buffer pH 4.5 for maximal stability. The control group was injected with the vehicle only. Development of DM was confirmed 48 hours later by the presence of glycosuria (>2000 mg/dl) along with polyuria. Rats with urine glucose values of <2000 mg/dL 24–48 hours after STZ injection were not considered to be diabetic and were excluded from further study.

steps.title: Induce myocardial infarction in rats
steps.instruction: Anesthetize male Sprague–Dawley rats (200–225 g) intraperitoneally with Nembutal 40 mg/kg; confirm adequate depth by lack of toe‑pinch response. Rapidly intubate and mechanically ventilate using a Harvard Apparatus Model 683 ventilator with tidal volume 1 ml per 100 g body weight and ventilation rate 65 strokes/min. Perform a left thoracotomy at the fourth intercostal space and permanently ligate the left anterior descending coronary artery with an irreversible tightening of a 6‑0 suture loop. Confirm myocardial infarction by regional cyanosis distal to the suture and ST‑segment elevation on ECG. Compress the chest cavity to evacuate air, then tightly seal the incision. Administer buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg subcutaneously pre‑operatively and repeat every 8–12 h for 48 h post‑operatively.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize with Nembutal 40 mg/kg IP; check toe‑pinch.
Intubate and ventilate: tidal volume 1 ml/100 g, 65 strokes/min, Model 683.
Ligate LAD with irreversible 6‑0 suture loop.
Confirm MI by cyanosis and ST‑elevation.
Compress chest to remove air, seal incision.
Give buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg SC pre‑op; repeat Q8–12 h for 48 h.

steps.title: Assess cardiac function by echocardiography
steps.instruction: Under light anesthesia, acquire transthoracic echocardiographic images with a Vevo 2100 (VisualSonics) scanner. Use M‑mode in the parasternal short‑axis view at the papillary‑muscle level to record LV fractional shortening (LVFS) and LV ejection fraction (LVEF). Record five consecutive cardiac cycles, average the measurements, and analyze offline with the scanner’s software by a blinded observer using standard formulas. Measure LV internal dimensions in diastole and systole (LVIDd, LVIDs) from M‑mode tracings at the mid‑papillary level according to modified ASE standards.

substeps.instruction: Image heart with Vevo 2100, parasternal short‑axis at papillary level.
Record M‑mode for LVFS and LVEF; capture five cycles.
Average values and analyze offline with software.
Measure LVIDd and LVIDs at mid‑papillary level per ASE standards.

steps.title: Measure blood glucose
steps.instruction: Collect a tail‑vein blood sample and determine glucose concentration using Accutrend Plus test strips and meter (Roche).

steps.title: Weigh lung and liver tissues
steps.instruction: Excise pieces of lung and liver, record wet weights, then place each sample in an oven at 65 °C until a constant weight is reached. Calculate wet‑to‑dry weight ratios for both organs.

substeps.instruction: Remove lung and liver pieces; weigh wet.
Dry samples at 65 °C until weight stabilizes.
